q: 1. The commonly used material in the manufacture of cement is
explain: Lime stone (calcareous material) supplies the required lime (CaO) content, which forms the major ingredient of cement, hence it is the commonly used raw material.

q: 2. The bulk density of aggregates is generally expressed as
explain: As per IS 2386, bulk density of aggregate is determined using a measuring cylinder of known litre capacity, so it is conventionally reported in kg per litre.

q: 3. Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured from
explain: OPC clinker is produced by burning a mixture of calcareous material (limestone) and argillaceous material (clay) in a kiln, then grinding with gypsum.

q: 4. In the manufacture of cement, the dry or wet mixture of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt at a temperature between
explain: In the kiln, the raw mixture of calcareous (limestone) and argillaceous (clay) materials is burnt at very high temperatures of about 1500°C to 1600°C to form clinker.

q: 5. The chemical ingredient of cement which provides quick setting property to the cement is
explain: Alumina in cement lowers the clinkering temperature and imparts quick setting properties, though excess alumina can weaken the cement.

q: 6. Sieve analysis of portland cement is performed on IS sieve No.
explain: Fineness of Portland cement is tested by sieving on IS Sieve No. 9 (90 micron sieve) as per Indian Standard specifications.

q: 7. The percentage of gypsum added to the clinker during manufacturing process is
explain: Gypsum is typically added in the range of 0.35% to 5.0% by weight of clinker to regulate the setting time of cement.

q: 8. Lime when added in excess quantity
options: caused the cement to expand and disintegrate
lowers the clinkering temperature of cement
explain: Excess free lime in cement remains uncombined, and upon hydration it expands, causing the cement to become unsound and disintegrate.

q: 9. The presence of dicalcium silicate in cement
options: has more resistance to sulphate attack
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly, generates less heat of hydration, and provides better resistance to sulphate attack, so all three statements apply.

q: 10. Increase in fineness modulus of aggregate indicates
explain: A higher fineness modulus value indicates that, on average, the aggregate particles are coarser, since FM is the sum of cumulative percentages retained on standard sieves divided by 100.

q: 11. The aggregate which pass through 4.75 mm IS sieve and entirely retain on 75 micron IS sieve is called
explain: Aggregate passing the 4.75mm sieve but retained on the 75-micron sieve is classified as fine aggregate.

q: 12. According to IS specifications for the compressive strength test of cement, the cement and sand mortar in the ratio of ......... is used
explain: As per IS 4031, the standard cement-sand mortar mix ratio used for the compressive strength test of cement is 1:3 (cement:standard sand).

q: 13. A good aggregate for concrete construction should be
explain: A good aggregate must simultaneously be chemically inert, strong, and hard/durable — all these properties together define suitability for concrete.

q: 14. The value of bulk density of aggregate depends upon
explain: Bulk density is influenced jointly by particle size distribution/grading, particle shape (affecting packing), and the specific gravity of the aggregate material — hence all of these factors matter.

q: 15. The maximum quantity of aggregate per 50 kg of cement should not exceed
explain: As per general guidelines, the total quantity of aggregate (fine plus coarse) used per 50kg bag of cement should not exceed about 450kg for good quality concrete.

q: 16. The bulk density of aggregates, is generally expressed as
explain: Bulk density of aggregates is conventionally expressed in kg/litre for practical field and laboratory measurement purposes.

q: 17. The type of aggregate of same nominal size, which contain less voids when compacted, are
explain: Rounded spherical aggregates pack more closely together, resulting in fewer voids compared to irregular or flaky shapes of the same nominal size.

q: 18. Bulking of sand is maximum if moisture content is about
explain: The bulking effect in sand is typically at its peak (maximum volume increase) at around 4% moisture content, before it decreases again as the sand becomes saturated.

q: 19. The bulk density of an aggregate does not depend upon
options: size and shape of the container
explain: Bulk density is a material property depending on aggregate size, shape, specific gravity, and grading — it does not depend on the size and shape of the measuring container.

q: 20. The bulk density of aggregates depends upon its
explain: Bulk density of aggregates is influenced together by particle shape, grading (size distribution), and the degree of compaction achieved during placement.

q: 21. The effect of creep on modular ratio is
options: either to decrease or to increase it
explain: Creep effectively reduces the modulus of elasticity of concrete over time, which increases the modular ratio (Es/Ec) used in design.

q: 22. Separation of water or water sand cement from a freshly concrete, is known
explain: Bleeding is the phenomenon where mixing water (sometimes carrying fine cement particles) rises to the surface of freshly placed concrete due to settlement of solids.

q: 23. Gap grading is one
options: In which one or more intermediate fractions are absent
In which the particles fall within a narrow limit of size fractions
In which combines different fractions of fine and coarse aggregate
In which all the particles are of uniform size
explain: Gap grading is defined by the deliberate omission of one or more intermediate particle-size fractions from the aggregate mix, unlike continuous grading which has all sizes present.

q: 24. Sands of zone I are
explain: As per IS 383 grading zone classification, Zone I represents the coarsest sand grading among the four zones.

q: 25. Vicat apparatus is not used for
explain: The Vicat apparatus is used for consistency and setting-time tests; compressive strength of cement is determined separately using a compression testing machine, not the Vicat apparatus.

q: 26. Shrinkage in cement concrete is directly proportional to
explain: Shrinkage of concrete is primarily caused by the loss of water from the cement paste, so it is directly proportional to the water content present in the mix.

q: 27. Vicat's apparatus is used for
explain: The Vicat apparatus (with the standard plunger) is primarily used to determine the standard/normal consistency of cement paste.

q: 28. Weight of an oven dry sand and air dry sand are 500 gm and 520 gm respectively. If the weight of the same sand under saturated but surface dry condition is 525 gm, then the water absorption of sand is
explain: Water absorption is calculated based on the oven-dry weight: (525 - 500)/500 × 100 = 5%, comparing SSD weight to the oven-dry weight.

q: 29. Soundness test of cement by Le-Chatelier's apparatus gives unsoundness due to
explain: The standard Le-Chatelier apparatus test specifically detects unsoundness caused by free (uncombined) lime present in the cement.

q: 30. Poisson's ratio for concrete ranges between
explain: The typical Poisson's ratio for concrete lies within the range of 0.11 to 0.21, depending on the mix and testing conditions.

q: 31. As compared to static tests the dynamic tests on concrete give
explain: Dynamic (vibration-based) testing methods generally yield a higher value of Poisson's ratio for concrete compared to static (load-based) testing methods.

q: 32. With increase in rate of loading during testing, compressive strength of concrete
explain: Concrete tested under a faster rate of loading shows an apparent increase in measured compressive strength, since there is less time for micro-crack propagation.

q: 33. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: according to the petrological characteristics, concrete aggregates are classified as heavy weight, normal weight and light weight
according to the shape of the particles, concrete aggregates are classified as rounded, irregular, angular and flaky
according to the surface texture of the particles, the concrete aggregates are classified as glossy, smooth, granular, rough, crystalline, honey combed and porous
explain: Aggregates can indeed be classified in all three ways simultaneously - by petrological characteristics (weight), by particle shape, and by surface texture - making all statements correct.

q: 34. The sieve number used in the fineness modules test of cement is
explain: Per the given answer key, sieve number 1 is used in the specified fineness modulus test procedure referenced in this question.

q: 35. In the manufacture of cement, the dry or wet mixture of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt in a
explain: The raw mix of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt in a rotary kiln, the standard equipment used in modern cement manufacture.

q: 36. In the manufacture of cement, the dry or wet mixture of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt in a .........
explain: The raw materials are burnt in the rotary kiln at a temperature range of about 1200°C to 1500°C to form clinker.

q: 37. The proportion of lime, silica, alumina and iron oxide in good Portland cement should be
explain: As per the standard composition given in this text, a good Portland cement should have lime, silica, alumina, and iron oxide roughly in the proportion 63:22:6:3.

q: 38. Le-Chatelier's apparatus is used for testing
explain: Le-Chatelier's apparatus is a standard test device specifically used to determine the soundness of cement, i.e., its tendency to undergo volume expansion after setting.

q: 39. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
explain: Using well-graded aggregate (a proper mix of different particle sizes) ensures minimum voids, better packing, and consequently higher-quality, denser concrete.

q: 40. The most useless aggregate is one whose surface texture is
explain: Glassy-textured aggregate provides very poor bond with the cement paste due to its smooth, non-porous, non-adherent surface, making it the least desirable for concrete.

q: 41. A concrete in which dry coarse aggregate are first packed to have the least voids and then the cement sand mortar is injected under pressure to fill all the voids, resulting in a very dense concrete, is known as
explain: This describes pre-packed concrete, where coarse aggregate is placed first and mortar is then grouted under pressure into the voids to produce a dense mass.

q: 42. Pozzolana is essentially a silicious material containing clay upto
explain: As defined in this text, pozzolana is a siliceous material that may contain clay content up to as much as 80%.

q: 43. Humidity causes ……… of cement in bag .
explain: Moisture in humid air can react with cement stored in bags, initiating premature hydration/setting reactions that spoil the cement before use.

q: 44. Soundness of the material means the resistance of the material against the effect of :
explain: Soundness specifically refers to a material's ability to resist volume changes/deterioration from repeated cycles of freezing and thawing.
